results.title: Associations of plasma omega-6 and omega-3 fatty acids with overall and 19 site-specific cancers: A population-based cohort study in UK Biobank.
results.reason: This prospective UK Biobank cohort reports an eligible human plasma biomarker exposure and incident prostate-cancer outcome with an adjusted hazard ratio, confidence interval, and recoverable case count.

extraction.comparison_type: Per 1-SD increase in plasma omega-3 fatty acids versus lower level
extraction.timing: Baseline plasma measurement with incident cancer follow-up
extraction.population: Adults aged 37–73 years without cancer at baseline

sample_size.excerpt: We investigated the associations of plasma omega-3 and omega-6 PUFAs with the incidence of overall and 19 site-specific cancers in a large prospective cohort. 253,138 eligible UK Biobank participants were included in our study.

effect_size.excerpt: Of the 19 site-specific cancers available, 14 were associated with omega-6% and five with omega-3%, all indicating inverse associations, with the exception that prostate cancer was positively associated with omega-3% (HR per SD = 1.03, 95% CI = 1.01-1.05).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Of the 19 site-specific cancers available, 14 were associated with omega-6% and five with omega-3%, all indicating inverse associations, with the exception that prostate cancer was positively associated with omega-3% (HR per SD = 1.03, 95% CI = 1.01-1.05).

p_value.excerpt: Only one site‐specific cancer, prostate cancer, was associated with omega‐3% (HR per SD = 1.03, 95% CI = 1.01–1.05, corrected p = .049) but not omega‐6% (HR per SD = 1.01, 95% CI = 0.98–1.03, corrected p = .56).
p_value.location: Results, Associations of plasma omega-6, omega-3, and their ratio with cancer risk, paragraph 3
